title: prefers-color-scheme
learningObjectives: Explain prefers-color-scheme and create motion that respects user preferences.

understand.concept: The prefers-color-scheme media feature detects whether the user prefers a light or dark colour scheme. CSS can adapt backgrounds, text, borders, and control styling while maintaining sufficient contrast.
understand.whyItMatters: Supporting colour-scheme preferences reduces unnecessary brightness and helps the interface fit user settings. Do not assume dark mode simply means inverting every colour.
understand.analogy: A theme preference is a presentation choice; the same content remains available in either palette.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual animation, rendering, and preference handling follow CSS and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The card uses a light default and switches to a dark palette when the user prefers dark mode.

examples.code:
Theme-aware card

The content remains the same in both themes.
examples.explanation: The card uses a light default and switches to a dark palette when the user prefers dark mode.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the animation or user-preference behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create light and dark styles for a card, form field, and focus indicator. Check contrast in both schemes.
practise.independentTask: Build a small motion-enhanced component. Provide a static or reduced-motion state and test the result with keyboard interaction.
hints: Keep essential content visible without animation.
Test light/dark and forced-colours preferences where relevant.
Measure performance on a representative device.

questions.prompt: Which media query detects the preferred light or dark theme?
questions.explanation: prefers-color-scheme reports the user's preferred colour scheme.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a user requests reduced motion?
options: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.answer: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.explanation: The interface should preserve content and operation while respecting the preference.
